publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the classification of cortical inhibitory interneurons and what their diversity is for
span.quote: Any meaningful classification scheme can only be based on function; therefore, differences in morphological (e.g., the number or laminar distribution of dendrites, the arborization pattern of axons, co-transmitter content, receptor expression pattern) or physiological features (e.g. firing pattern, short- and long-term synaptic plasticity) should be used to generate new cell types only if these differences are causally linked to a functional dichotomy.

span.label: which measurable differences between interneurons should be allowed to define distinct cell types
span.quote: However, the same question arises here as in case of morphological details, i.e., which characteristics are relevant from a functional point of view, which are those that evolved as an adaptive property to enable the cell type to fulfil its job more efficiently, and which are those that exist simply as a side product, but survive similarly to natural mutations, which are abundant in the genome of any living creature.

span.label: sets a functional criterion for admitting new interneuron types, organises the known classes by input source and target compartment, and reports the in vivo evidence that anatomically defined classes are functionally homogeneous
span.quote: The results of these studies indicated that each anatomically/neurochemically defined cell type had characteristic (e.g., phase-locked) firing patterns relative to theta and gamma oscillations and sharp-wave-associated ripples (see below for cell-type-specific details), consistent with a functionally homogeneous role of each anatomical class in the generation of population activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Interneurons innervating somata, proximal dendrites or axon initial segments (the Perisomatic Inhibitory cells) are specialized to control output from large principal cell populations, and one of their main functions is to rhythmically synchronize principal cell activity at theta (4-8 Hz) and gamma (30-100 Hz) frequencies.

span.label: cortical inhibitory interneurons
span.quote: Inhibition in cortical networks is supplied by a wide range of interneuron types that subserve different functions, and possess specific connectivity features, morphological, electrophysiological and neurochemical characteristics that enable them to fulfil these roles.

span.label: review
span.quote: In the sections below, the two largest classes of cortical interneurons (i.e., perisomatic and dendritic inhibitory cells) will be described in more detail, based mostly on data from the hippocampus, but with an emphasis on features that can be generalized to the entire cerebral cortex.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Kv3-family potassium channel expression gives parvalbumin basket cells their fast-spiking phenotype, which is what allows them to respond with minimal delay and sustain high-frequency firing
span.quote: For instance, parvalbumin-containing basket cells express voltage-gated potassium channels of the Kv3 family, which contributes essentially to the "fast-spiking" behavior of these neurons, allowing them to respond to incoming synaptic input with minimal delay, and to sustain high-frequency spiking activity in response to strong input.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: interneuron-driven synchronization of principal cell firing produces coincident spikes, which are a more effective trigger of firing downstream and therefore raise transmission efficiency
span.quote: This may enhance the efficiency of information transmission by increasing the likelihood of coincident spiking, which is an effective trigger of action potential firing in downstream neurons.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: synchronized principal cell firing facilitates synaptic potentiation and thereby the formation of the potentiated cell ensembles that carry memory traces
span.quote: The outcome of interneuron activity is often synchronization of firing in large principal cell populations, which facilitates synaptic potentiation (enhancement of synaptic efficacy) and the formation of potentiated cell ensembles or networks as correlates of memory traces.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: O-LM feed-back inhibition blocks plasticity of entorhinal inputs at the theta trough, but pyramidal cells firing ahead of the population in phase precession escape that inhibition and so can potentiate their inputs
span.quote: However, when pyramidal cells fire in phase precession mode, ahead of the population firing – this happens when they are conveying specific signals e.g. by place field-dependent firing – they can escape feed-back inhibition from the O-LM cells, and their entorhinal input synapses can be potentiated.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: feed-forward and feed-back inhibition reduce the number of simultaneously active principal cells, producing sparse representations useful for sensory coding and long-term memory
span.quote: At the network level, both feed-forward and feed-back inhibition act to reduce the number of simultaneously active principal cells, working towards the creation of sparse representations (Acsády and Káli, 2007), which are thought to be advantageous for both sensory processing (Olshausen and Field, 2004) and long-term memory (Treves and Rolls, 1994).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: feedback inhibition sets up winner-take-all competition among principal cells, so that one cell's increased activity suppresses its neighbours
span.quote: Feedback inhibition also introduces direct competition among members of a local principal cell population, whereby an increase in the activity of one cell tends to decrease the activity of its fellows.

span.label: a rule is stated for when a measured difference may create a new category: only when it is causally linked to a functional dichotomy
span.quote: Any meaningful classification scheme can only be based on function; therefore, differences in morphological (e.g., the number or laminar distribution of dendrites, the arborization pattern of axons, co-transmitter content, receptor expression pattern) or physiological features (e.g. firing pattern, short- and long-term synaptic plasticity) should be used to generate new cell types only if these differences are causally linked to a functional dichotomy.

span.label: the failure mode of dropping that rule is named - admitting every measurable feature yields an astronomical number of types
span.quote: These results have led some to propose that a functional cell class may only be fully determined by a conjunction of anatomical and physiological features, leading to a potentially astronomical number of functionally distinct cell types (see Markram et al., 2004).

span.label: the discriminating question is put in evolutionary terms: which features are adaptations for the job and which are side products that merely survived
span.quote: However, the same question arises here as in case of morphological details, i.e., which characteristics are relevant from a functional point of view, which are those that evolved as an adaptive property to enable the cell type to fulfil its job more efficiently, and which are those that exist simply as a side product, but survive similarly to natural mutations, which are abundant in the genome of any living creature.

span.label: the classification is built from input-output properties, because those determine the morphology rather than the other way round
span.quote: For a functional classification, the most important features are the input-output properties, i.e. the identity of afferents driving a particular cell type, and the sites where these cells exert their inhibitory effects.

span.label: the tree is then branched twice - first by whether the target is another interneuron, then by which compartment of the principal cell is targeted
span.quote: The next major branching in the classification scheme of interneurons is determined by the principal cell compartment which they target , since inhibition targeting pyramidal cell dendrites is functionally distinct from inhibition that primarily affects the perisomatic region.

span.label: the anatomical taxonomy is checked against an independent criterion: firing phase relative to naturally occurring population rhythms in vivo
span.quote: Importantly, the discharge patterns of neurons in relation to these naturally occurring population events offer a powerful and functionally relevant way of classifying cortical interneurons.

span.label: and passes, with each anatomically defined class showing characteristic phase-locked patterns
span.quote: The results of these studies indicated that each anatomically/neurochemically defined cell type had characteristic (e.g., phase-locked) firing patterns relative to theta and gamma oscillations and sharp-wave-associated ripples (see below for cell-type-specific details), consistent with a functionally homogeneous role of each anatomical class in the generation of population activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).

span.label: a simpler homologous system is chosen for dissection precisely because its lamination lets connectivity be read off position
span.quote: A simpler version of cortical architecture can be found in the hippocampus , where the fundamental principles of interneuronal connectivity are the same as in the neocortex, but due to the simple lamination, these circuits can be dissected and the functional roles extrapolated with greater precision.

span.label: the possibility that the observed diversity is an artefact of the slice preparation is raised rather than assumed away
span.quote: In addition, at least some of the differences seen in physiological behavior may result from the artificial recording conditions in vitro, and a different classification or even more homogeneous responses might result from the conditions (including the concentrations of metabotropically active neurotransmitters and the rates and patterns of excitatory and inhibitory synaptic input) experienced by cortical interneurons in the behaving animal.

span.label: two named types are flagged as possibly one type with an unlabelled axon
span.quote: There are reports of so-called backprojection neurons, which innervate all hippocampal subfields, form synapses primarily with principal cells, and are very similar to the HS cells. They may in fact also be HS cells whose septally projecting axon was accidentally not labelled.

span.label: a continuum between two axonal arbour patterns is acknowledged where the scheme wants discrete types
span.quote: The axon of a subtype is confined to stratum radiatum only, and there seems to be a continuum between this subtype and the classical bistratified arbours with a varying size of a stratum oriens component.

span.label: the compartment logic is derived from function: dendrites are where plasticity happens, the perisomatic region is where output is decided
span.quote: Thus, interneurons innervating principal cell dendrites (the Dendritic Inhibitory cells) are designed to control the efficacy and most notably the plasticity of excitatory inputs to principal cells.

span.label: Direct evidence about what interneurons actually do in cortical computation is scarce relative to descriptive anatomical and physiological data.
span.quote: Compared to the abundance of information on the morphological, physiological, and molecular properties of interneurons and their synaptic connections, there is still a relative paucity of direct information on the functional roles of interneurons in cortical computations

span.label: Physiological classifications may be artefacts of in vitro recording conditions rather than properties of interneurons in the behaving animal.
span.quote: In addition, at least some of the differences seen in physiological behavior may result from the artificial recording conditions in vitro, and a different classification or even more homogeneous responses might result from the conditions (including the concentrations of metabotropically active neurotransmitters and the rates and patterns of excitatory and inhibitory synaptic input) experienced by cortical interneurons in the behaving animal.

span.label: The molecular identity of at least one reviewed cell class is unsettled.
span.quote: The molecular characteristics of this cell type are controversial, but may include the expression of CB and/or PV.

span.label: the criterion demands function, and direct functional evidence is admitted to be scarce
span.quote: Compared to the abundance of information on the morphological, physiological, and molecular properties of interneurons and their synaptic connections, there is still a relative paucity of direct information on the functional roles of interneurons in cortical computations

span.label: the functions of the neocortical dendritic-inhibitory types in particular have been hard to identify
span.quote: However, the precise functions of these neocortical cell types have been difficult to identify.

span.label: some physiological diversity may be an artefact of in vitro recording conditions
span.quote: In addition, at least some of the differences seen in physiological behavior may result from the artificial recording conditions in vitro, and a different classification or even more homogeneous responses might result from the conditions (including the concentrations of metabotropically active neurotransmitters and the rates and patterns of excitatory and inhibitory synaptic input) experienced by cortical interneurons in the behaving animal.

span.label: the molecular characterisation of bistratified cells is contested
span.quote: The molecular characteristics of this cell type are controversial, but may include the expression of CB and/or PV.

span.label: the stabilisation account of interneuron function is described by the authors as simplistic where epilepsy is concerned
span.quote: This notion also offers a simplistic explanation for the critical involvement of interneurons in epilepsy

span.label: a single dendritic inhibitory cell contributes negligibly on its own, so claims about their function require synchrony that is not always demonstrated
span.quote: Individual dendritic inhibitory cells of any type provide 2 to 20 synapses onto a single target pyramidal cell, which are scattered all over the dendritic tree. Thus, the contribution of a single dendritic inhibitory cell to the control of dendritic functions of principal cells is likely to be negligible. Thus, they have to fire in synchrony.

span.label: the adaptation versus neutral side-product distinction, imported as the test for whether a measured feature may define a cell type
span.quote: However, the same question arises here as in case of morphological details, i.e., which characteristics are relevant from a functional point of view, which are those that evolved as an adaptive property to enable the cell type to fulfil its job more efficiently, and which are those that exist simply as a side product, but survive similarly to natural mutations, which are abundant in the genome of any living creature.

span.label: the impedance profile and resonance, used to explain why particular cell classes participate in particular frequency bands
span.quote: Some neuronal classes show distinct peaks (" resonances ") in their impedance profiles at characteristic frequencies, which may contribute to their differential involvement in the generation of network oscillations in various frequency bands.

span.label: sparse representation as a design goal, imported to give feed-forward and feed-back inhibition a shared computational purpose
span.quote: At the network level, both feed-forward and feed-back inhibition act to reduce the number of simultaneously active principal cells, working towards the creation of sparse representations (Acsády and Káli, 2007), which are thought to be advantageous for both sensory processing (Olshausen and Field, 2004) and long-term memory (Treves and Rolls, 1994).

span.label: interneuron - defined by local axons, versus the class called long-range interneurons which explicitly fails that definition and keeps the name anyway
span.quote: Although these neurons, by virtue of the existence of their long-range projections, do not meet the definition of interneuron given at the beginning of this article, they can probably fulfil similar roles within the local network through their short-range axon collaterals, and are therefore commonly referred to as "long-range interneurons

span.label: a cell type - as any reproducible difference in morphology or physiology, versus only those differences causally tied to a functional dichotomy; the article insists on the second
span.quote: Any meaningful classification scheme can only be based on function; therefore, differences in morphological (e.g., the number or laminar distribution of dendrites, the arborization pattern of axons, co-transmitter content, receptor expression pattern) or physiological features (e.g. firing pattern, short- and long-term synaptic plasticity) should be used to generate new cell types only if these differences are causally linked to a functional dichotomy.

span.label: a measured feature - as an adaptation for the cell's job versus as a surviving side product; the distinction that decides whether it may define a type
span.quote: However, the same question arises here as in case of morphological details, i.e., which characteristics are relevant from a functional point of view, which are those that evolved as an adaptive property to enable the cell type to fulfil its job more efficiently, and which are those that exist simply as a side product, but survive similarly to natural mutations, which are abundant in the genome of any living creature.

span.label: inhibition - feed-forward, driven from outside the target territory, versus feed-back, driven by the very population it inhibits
span.quote: The dominant excitatory drive of interneurons may originate from outside the territory (i.e., area/subfield/layer) of their neuronal targets, in which case they are said to mediate feed-forward inhibition. Conversely, if the dominant source of input to an interneuron is the same population of cells which is targeted by the interneuron, it is considered to provide feed-back inhibition (Figure 1).

span.label: inhibitory target - dendritic, controlling plasticity of incoming excitation, versus perisomatic, controlling whether output is generated at all
span.quote: The next major branching in the classification scheme of interneurons is determined by the principal cell compartment which they target , since inhibition targeting pyramidal cell dendrites is functionally distinct from inhibition that primarily affects the perisomatic region.

span.label: GABAergic effect - hyperpolarising in general, but possibly depolarising at the axon initial segment, which would reverse what axo-axonic cells do
span.quote: However, recent evidence suggests that their postsynaptic GABAA -receptor-mediated effect may be depolarizing, and, as a consequence, they may be able to discharge the entire pyramidal cell population they innervate, with the aim of synchronizing their output, or to reset conductances in their dendritic trees.

span.label: physiological classification - as measured in vitro versus as it might appear in the behaving animal; the first may create diversity the second would not show
span.quote: In addition, at least some of the differences seen in physiological behavior may result from the artificial recording conditions in vitro, and a different classification or even more homogeneous responses might result from the conditions (including the concentrations of metabotropically active neurotransmitters and the rates and patterns of excitatory and inhibitory synaptic input) experienced by cortical interneurons in the behaving animal.

span.label: builds-on → Freund (2003)
span.quote: A synthesis of the above features led to the proposal (Freund, 2003) that the electrically and synaptically coupled, and mostly locally driven, ensembles of PV-containing basket cells are indispensable components of the oscillating cortical hardware; they represent a precision clockwork without which no cortical operations are possible.

span.label: critiques → classification schemes that generate cell types from any measurable morphological or physiological difference
span.quote: Any meaningful classification scheme can only be based on function; therefore, differences in morphological (e.g., the number or laminar distribution of dendrites, the arborization pattern of axons, co-transmitter content, receptor expression pattern) or physiological features (e.g. firing pattern, short- and long-term synaptic plasticity) should be used to generate new cell types only if these differences are causally linked to a functional dichotomy.

span.label: critiques → the proposal that a functional cell class requires a conjunction of anatomical and physiological features, which would give an astronomical number of types
span.quote: These results have led some to propose that a functional cell class may only be fully determined by a conjunction of anatomical and physiological features, leading to a potentially astronomical number of functionally distinct cell types (see Markram et al., 2004).

span.label: supports → Somogyi and Klausberger, that anatomically and neurochemically defined classes are functionally homogeneous in vivo
span.quote: The results of these studies indicated that each anatomically/neurochemically defined cell type had characteristic (e.g., phase-locked) firing patterns relative to theta and gamma oscillations and sharp-wave-associated ripples (see below for cell-type-specific details), consistent with a functionally homogeneous role of each anatomical class in the generation of population activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).

span.label: builds-on → Freund and Buzsaki and subsequent reviews of interneuron diversity
span.quote: Any meaningful classification scheme can only be based on function; therefore, differences in morphological (e.g., the number or laminar distribution of dendrites, the arborization pattern of axons, co-transmitter content, receptor expression pattern) or physiological features (e.g. firing pattern, short- and long-term synaptic plasticity) should be used to generate new cell types only if these differences are causally linked to a functional dichotomy.

span.label: supports → the proposal that PV basket cell ensembles are the indispensable clockwork of cortical oscillation, with CCK ensembles superimposed as a tuning system
span.quote: A synthesis of the above features led to the proposal (Freund, 2003) that the electrically and synaptically coupled, and mostly locally driven, ensembles of PV-containing basket cells are indispensable components of the oscillating cortical hardware; they represent a precision clockwork without which no cortical operations are possible.

span.label: critiques → the simple runaway-excitation account of interneuron function as an explanation of epilepsy
span.quote: This notion also offers a simplistic explanation for the critical involvement of interneurons in epilepsy

span.label: Interneurons —contrasted-with→ principal cells
span.quote: Interneurons are types of nerve cells, typically found in integrative areas of the central nervous system , whose axons (and dendrites) are limited to a single brain area. This feature distinguishes them from principal cells, which often have axonal projections outside the brain area where their cell bodies and dendrites are located.

span.label: feed-forward inhibition —contrasted-with→ feed-back inhibition
span.quote: The dominant excitatory drive of interneurons may originate from outside the territory (i.e., area/subfield/layer) of their neuronal targets, in which case they are said to mediate feed-forward inhibition. Conversely, if the dominant source of input to an interneuron is the same population of cells which is targeted by the interneuron, it is considered to provide feed-back inhibition (Figure 1).

span.label: Perisomatic Inhibitory cells —contrasted-with→ Dendritic Inhibitory cells
span.quote: The next major branching in the classification scheme of interneurons is determined by the principal cell compartment which they target , since inhibition targeting pyramidal cell dendrites is functionally distinct from inhibition that primarily affects the perisomatic region.

span.label: Interneuron-Selective interneurons —part-of→ Interneurons
span.quote: This represents the first dichotomy in the classification scheme, since there are subsets of interneurons containing the calcium binding protein calretinin (CR), or the neuropeptide vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP), which were shown to form synapses predominantly on other GABAergic cells, and were therefore termed Interneuron-Selective interneurons (or IS cells).

span.label: axo-axonic —part-of→ Perisomatic Inhibitory cells
span.quote: Interneurons innervating somata, proximal dendrites or axon initial segments (the Perisomatic Inhibitory cells) are specialized to control output from large principal cell populations, and one of their main functions is to rhythmically synchronize principal cell activity at theta (4-8 Hz) and gamma (30-100 Hz) frequencies.

span.label: basket cells —part-of→ Perisomatic Inhibitory cells
span.quote: The remaining types of Perisomatic Inhibitory cells are basket cells that form multiple synaptic contacts on the somata and proximal dendrites of principal cells, each basket cell targeting about 1500-2000 of them.

span.label: O-LM —part-of→ Dendritic Inhibitory cells
span.quote: Distinct types of dendritic interneurons have evolved to control glutamatergic inputs of principal cells from different sources. The so-called Oriens – Lacunosum-Moleculare (O-LM) interneurons selectively terminate in stratum lacunosum-moleculare in conjunction with excitatory input coming from the entorhinal cortex

span.label: parvalbumin —contrasted-with→ cholecystokinin
span.quote: The two major subtypes of hippocampal basket cell can be distinguished easiest on the basis of their neuropeptide/calcium binding protein content; however, this neurochemical difference is coupled to functionally more meaningful unique features related to synaptic inputs and receptor expression patterns.

span.label: Perisomatic Inhibitory cells —causes→ gamma
span.quote: Interneurons innervating somata, proximal dendrites or axon initial segments (the Perisomatic Inhibitory cells) are specialized to control output from large principal cell populations, and one of their main functions is to rhythmically synchronize principal cell activity at theta (4-8 Hz) and gamma (30-100 Hz) frequencies.

span.label: long-range interneurons —distinct-from→ Interneurons
span.quote: Although these neurons, by virtue of the existence of their long-range projections, do not meet the definition of interneuron given at the beginning of this article, they can probably fulfil similar roles within the local network through their short-range axon collaterals, and are therefore commonly referred to as "long-range interneurons

span.label: Interneurons —causes→ sparse representations
span.quote: At the network level, both feed-forward and feed-back inhibition act to reduce the number of simultaneously active principal cells, working towards the creation of sparse representations (Acsády and Káli, 2007), which are thought to be advantageous for both sensory processing (Olshausen and Field, 2004) and long-term memory (Treves and Rolls, 1994).

span.label: The article argues that interneuron classification is only meaningful when morphological or physiological differences map onto a functional dichotomy, rather than being catalogued for their own sake.
span.quote: Any meaningful classification scheme can only be based on function; therefore, differences in morphological (e.g., the number or laminar distribution of dendrites, the arborization pattern of axons, co-transmitter content, receptor expression pattern) or physiological features (e.g. firing pattern, short- and long-term synaptic plasticity) should be used to generate new cell types only if these differences are causally linked to a functional dichotomy.

span.label: Interneuron diversity scales with the complexity of the local network, which is why the six-layered neocortex hosts the greatest variety of interneuron types.
span.quote: Diversity of interneurons , both in terms of structure and function, increases with the complexity of local networks within a given brain area, and this likely correlates with the complexity of the functions carried out by that brain area.

span.label: In vivo recordings from anatomically identified cells show each anatomical/neurochemical class has its own characteristic phase relationship to theta, gamma and ripples, supporting functional homogeneity of the anatomical classes.
span.quote: The results of these studies indicated that each anatomically/neurochemically defined cell type had characteristic (e.g., phase-locked) firing patterns relative to theta and gamma oscillations and sharp-wave-associated ripples (see below for cell-type-specific details), consistent with a functionally homogeneous role of each anatomical class in the generation of population activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).

span.label: Parvalbumin and cholecystokinin basket cells divide the labour: PV cells increase firing during sharp waves while CCK cells do not, reflecting their different feed-forward versus feed-back drives.
span.quote: While PV cells strongly increase their firing during sharp waves, CCK cell discharges remain unchanged.

span.label: The article advances the proposal that PV basket cell ensembles are the obligatory oscillatory 'clockwork' of cortex, with CCK ensembles superimposed as a modulatory layer.
span.quote: A synthesis of the above features led to the proposal (Freund, 2003) that the electrically and synaptically coupled, and mostly locally driven, ensembles of PV-containing basket cells are indispensable components of the oscillating cortical hardware; they represent a precision clockwork without which no cortical operations are possible.

span.label: Newly described ivy cells, marked by nitric oxide synthase and neuropeptide Y, may outnumber parvalbumin cells and thus displace them as the most abundant hippocampal interneuron.
span.quote: Cells of this type are suggested to be more numerous than parvalbumin-expressing neurons (previously thought to be the most abundant type of hippocampal interneuron), and are characterized by the expression of the enzyme nitric oxide synthase together with neuropeptide Y.

span.label: Because any single dendritic inhibitory cell contributes only a handful of scattered synapses per pyramidal cell, dendritic inhibition can only be effective if these cells fire synchronously.
span.quote: Thus, the contribution of a single dendritic inhibitory cell to the control of dendritic functions of principal cells is likely to be negligible.

span.label: each anatomically and neurochemically defined class has characteristic phase-locked firing relative to theta, gamma and ripples
span.quote: The results of these studies indicated that each anatomically/neurochemically defined cell type had characteristic (e.g., phase-locked) firing patterns relative to theta and gamma oscillations and sharp-wave-associated ripples (see below for cell-type-specific details), consistent with a functionally homogeneous role of each anatomical class in the generation of population activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).

span.label: PV and CCK basket cells fire at the theta peak but with opposite phase shifts, and diverge during sharp waves
span.quote: Although both basket cell types are primarily responsible for rhythmic synchronization of the activity of large principal cell populations at theta and gamma frequencies, there is a considerable division of labour between them associated with their differential behaviour during sharp waves, and with different excitatory drives.

span.label: PV basket cells are driven mainly feed-forward while CCK basket cells require combined feed-back and feed-forward drive
span.quote: CCK basket cells generally receive far less local glutamatergic inputs than PV cells, but are selectively innervated by serotonergic afferents from the median raphe via 5HT3 receptors.

span.label: each axo-axonic cell contacts the axon initial segments of about 1000-1500 pyramidal cells
span.quote: Axo-axonic, or chandelier cells innervate exclusively the axon initial segments of principal cells, and occur both in the hippocampus and in the neocortex.

span.label: each basket cell targets about 1500-2000 principal cells
span.quote: The remaining types of Perisomatic Inhibitory cells are basket cells that form multiple synaptic contacts on the somata and proximal dendrites of principal cells, each basket cell targeting about 1500-2000 of them.

span.label: axo-axonic GABA-A effects may be depolarising, which would make them synchronisers rather than silencers
span.quote: However, recent evidence suggests that their postsynaptic GABAA -receptor-mediated effect may be depolarizing, and, as a consequence, they may be able to discharge the entire pyramidal cell population they innervate, with the aim of synchronizing their output, or to reset conductances in their dendritic trees.

span.label: PV basket cells express Kv3 channels, which underlie fast-spiking and minimal response delay
span.quote: For instance, parvalbumin-containing basket cells express voltage-gated potassium channels of the Kv3 family, which contributes essentially to the "fast-spiking" behavior of these neurons, allowing them to respond to incoming synaptic input with minimal delay, and to sustain high-frequency spiking activity in response to strong input.

span.label: Ivy cells may be more numerous than PV cells, previously thought the most abundant hippocampal interneuron
span.quote: Cells of this type are suggested to be more numerous than parvalbumin-expressing neurons (previously thought to be the most abundant type of hippocampal interneuron), and are characterized by the expression of the enzyme nitric oxide synthase together with neuropeptide Y.

span.label: a single dendritic inhibitory cell makes only 2 to 20 synapses on a target pyramidal cell, so these cells must act in synchrony
span.quote: Individual dendritic inhibitory cells of any type provide 2 to 20 synapses onto a single target pyramidal cell, which are scattered all over the dendritic tree. Thus, the contribution of a single dendritic inhibitory cell to the control of dendritic functions of principal cells is likely to be negligible. Thus, they have to fire in synchrony.

span.label: O-LM cells may block plasticity of entorhinal input exactly when most local pyramidal cells fire, while phase-precessing cells escape that inhibition
span.quote: However, when pyramidal cells fire in phase precession mode, ahead of the population firing – this happens when they are conveying specific signals e.g. by place field-dependent firing – they can escape feed-back inhibition from the O-LM cells, and their entorhinal input synapses can be potentiated.

span.label: HS cells have unusually long dendrites, consistent with monitoring global population synchrony and relaying it to septal pacemakers
span.quote: The dendrites are extremely long, suggesting that the neuron is sampling input from a large population of local principal cells, apparently monitoring the level of global population synchrony.

span.label: interneuron diversity increases with the complexity of the local network, and the six-layered neocortex has the most types
span.quote: Diversity of interneurons , both in terms of structure and function, increases with the complexity of local networks within a given brain area, and this likely correlates with the complexity of the functions carried out by that brain area.

This feature distinguishes them from principal cells, which often have axonal projections outside the brain area where their cell bodies and dendrites are located.

span.label: feed-forward
span.quote: The dominant excitatory drive of interneurons may originate from outside the territory (i.e., area/subfield/layer) of their neuronal targets, in which case they are said to mediate feed-forward inhibition. Conversely, if the dominant source of input to an interneuron is the same population of cells which is targeted by the interneuron, it is considered to provide feed-back inhibition (Figure 1).

span.label: Interneuron-Selective interneurons
span.quote: This represents the first dichotomy in the classification scheme, since there are subsets of interneurons containing the calcium binding protein calretinin (CR), or the neuropeptide vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP), which were shown to form synapses predominantly on other GABAergic cells, and were therefore termed Interneuron-Selective interneurons (or IS cells).

span.label: axo-axonic
span.quote: Axo-axonic, or chandelier cells innervate exclusively the axon initial segments of principal cells, and occur both in the hippocampus and in the neocortex.

span.label: phase precession
span.quote: Oscillatory activity in neuronal populations can also serve as a temporal reference signal for phase encoding, a form of temporal coding where the timing of action potentials with respect to the phase of an ongoing oscillation carries information.

span.label: long-range interneurons
span.quote: Although these neurons, by virtue of the existence of their long-range projections, do not meet the definition of interneuron given at the beginning of this article, they can probably fulfil similar roles within the local network through their short-range axon collaterals, and are therefore commonly referred to as "long-range interneurons

span.label: 1000-1500 — number of pyramidal cell axon initial segments innervated by a single axo-axonic (chandelier) cell
span.quote: Each axo-axonic cell forms radially running rows of boutons that climb along the axon initial segments of about 1000-1500 pyramidal cells.

span.label: 1500-2000 — number of principal cells whose somata and proximal dendrites a single basket cell targets
span.quote: The remaining types of Perisomatic Inhibitory cells are basket cells that form multiple synaptic contacts on the somata and proximal dendrites of principal cells, each basket cell targeting about 1500-2000 of them.

span.label: 2 to 20 — number of synapses a single dendritic inhibitory cell makes onto one target pyramidal cell
span.quote: Individual dendritic inhibitory cells of any type provide 2 to 20 synapses onto a single target pyramidal cell, which are scattered all over the dendritic tree.

span.label: 4-8 Hz and 30-100 Hz — the theta and gamma frequency bands at which perisomatic inhibitory cells rhythmically synchronize principal cell activity
span.quote: Interneurons innervating somata, proximal dendrites or axon initial segments (the Perisomatic Inhibitory cells) are specialized to control output from large principal cell populations, and one of their main functions is to rhythmically synchronize principal cell activity at theta (4-8 Hz) and gamma (30-100 Hz) frequencies.

span.label: 800 to 1,700 µm — measured extent of axonal arbours of intracellularly labelled hippocampal axo-axonic cells
span.quote: Intracellularly labelled axo-axonic cells in the hippocampus had axonal arbours measuring 800 to 1,700 µm.

span.label: at least three times — how much more glutamatergic synaptic input PV basket cells receive relative to CCK basket cells
span.quote: PV cells have at least three times more glutamatergic synaptic (mostly Schaffer collateral) inputs than CCK cells, whereas the latter receive serotonergic input from the median raphe and express 5-HT3, nicotinic a7 and a4 receptors.

span.label: about 400 by 800 µm — area covered by the axonal arbour of an O-LM interneuron in the transverse and longitudinal planes
span.quote: The axonal arbour of O-LM cells is rather focused in the transverse plane, and elongated in the longitudinal direction, covering an area of about 400 by 800 µm.

span.label: about 1 mm — transverse extent of hippocampal basket cell axonal arbours
span.quote: The transverse extent of basket cell axonal arbours in the hippocampus was found to be about 1 mm.

span.label: 1000-1500 pyramidal cells — axon initial segments contacted by one axo-axonic cell
span.quote: Axo-axonic, or chandelier cells innervate exclusively the axon initial segments of principal cells, and occur both in the hippocampus and in the neocortex.

span.label: 1500-2000 — principal cells targeted by one basket cell
span.quote: The remaining types of Perisomatic Inhibitory cells are basket cells that form multiple synaptic contacts on the somata and proximal dendrites of principal cells, each basket cell targeting about 1500-2000 of them.

span.label: theta (4-8 Hz) and gamma (30-100 Hz) — the frequency bands perisomatic cells synchronise
span.quote: Interneurons innervating somata, proximal dendrites or axon initial segments (the Perisomatic Inhibitory cells) are specialized to control output from large principal cell populations, and one of their main functions is to rhythmically synchronize principal cell activity at theta (4-8 Hz) and gamma (30-100 Hz) frequencies.

span.label: 2 to 20 synapses — contacts made by one dendritic inhibitory cell on one pyramidal cell
span.quote: Individual dendritic inhibitory cells of any type provide 2 to 20 synapses onto a single target pyramidal cell, which are scattered all over the dendritic tree. Thus, the contribution of a single dendritic inhibitory cell to the control of dendritic functions of principal cells is likely to be negligible. Thus, they have to fire in synchrony.

span.label: 800 to 1,700 µm — axonal arbour extent of labelled hippocampal axo-axonic cells
span.quote: Axo-axonic, or chandelier cells innervate exclusively the axon initial segments of principal cells, and occur both in the hippocampus and in the neocortex.

span.label: phase-locked
span.quote: The results of these studies indicated that each anatomically/neurochemically defined cell type had characteristic (e.g., phase-locked) firing patterns relative to theta and gamma oscillations and sharp-wave-associated ripples (see below for cell-type-specific details), consistent with a functionally homogeneous role of each anatomical class in the generation of population activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).

span.label: impedance profile
span.quote: Some neuronal classes show distinct peaks (" resonances ") in their impedance profiles at characteristic frequencies, which may contribute to their differential involvement in the generation of network oscillations in various frequency bands.

span.label: firing pattern
span.quote: Importantly, the discharge patterns of neurons in relation to these naturally occurring population events offer a powerful and functionally relevant way of classifying cortical interneurons.

span.label: target compartment
span.quote: The next major branching in the classification scheme of interneurons is determined by the principal cell compartment which they target , since inhibition targeting pyramidal cell dendrites is functionally distinct from inhibition that primarily affects the perisomatic region.

span.label: calcium binding protein content
span.quote: The two major subtypes of hippocampal basket cell can be distinguished easiest on the basis of their neuropeptide/calcium binding protein content; however, this neurochemical difference is coupled to functionally more meaningful unique features related to synaptic inputs and receptor expression patterns.
